items.q: What should you remember about **Market > execution when stuck**?
items.a: **local optimum on a small** hill ($50–100M) vs trillion-dollar mountain; SDR-only plays are a Bay Area mirage.

items.q: What should you remember about **Category creation is a long game**?
items.a: **unique product first; category** emerges only after copycats; no existing budget line at start.

items.q: What should you remember about **CRM captures ~1%**?
items.a: **rest lives in heads/calls;** autonomous capture was the 2016 thesis before "AI" was mainstream.

items.q: What should you remember about **Customer obsession, not competitor matching**?
items.a: **in expansive early markets,** hunt Easter eggs; don't mirror rival feature bundles (2023 trap).

items.q: What should you remember about **Cash + engineering > office trophies**?
items.a: **barely touched raised capital;** WeWork/short leases; invest in people when sector struggles.

items.q: What should you remember about **Attack when rivals are gasping**?
items.a: **cycling climb metaphor**: accelerate into competitor exhaustion; shipped 4 product lines while bundles stalled.

items.q: What should you remember about **Vibe-coding moat skepticism**?
items.a: **code leak ≠ runnable** enterprise; CRM/HR/revenue ops need 10-year operational complexity + trust.

items.q: What should you remember about **Sales AI is hard**?
items.a: **asymmetrical buyer engagement, deception,** politics, judgment/creativity beyond plausible-token outputs.

items.q: What should you remember about **Raving fans > happy customers**?
items.a: **mission is outcome (revenue** potential), not feature checklist; product must surprise repeatedly.

items.q: What should you remember about **Layer revenue S-curves early**?
items.a: **each source hits glass** ceiling; plan next curve before current one flatlines.
